items.name_html: archive is not the preservation path
items.body_html: audit / metrics / eval are computed from the durable run record (or the surviving global metrics stream), never from an archive. Archive / export is an optional cold copy; deleting all archives changes no correctness property. Naming archive-as-preservation reimports the v1 mental model

no dangling refs (the LC1 INV-3 payoff; the v1 evidence-loss bug is impossible) — a hard purge removes the full run record and exactly the closure-owned T3 blobs (mechanics in the contract + ordering tables)

items.name_html: the destructive precondition is on the purge, not the intent
items.body_html: DELETE_REQUESTED is accepted on a live run (with force) and drives cancel → LC2 release → purge; the irreversible hard_purge commit runs only when terminal && release discharged (else deferred). So the operator can start the chain early, but nothing is destroyed before the run is wound down

items.name_html: a purge leaves a tombstone; the global audit survives
items.body_html: a purged run survives only as its run_index tombstone — the authority for purged (there is no instance.purge_state ← purged; see the state authority table) — plus the self-contained global metrics/audit stream (the coarse audit floor). The full canonical run record is gone

items.name_html: delete is an operator intent, not a workflow action
items.body_html: DELETE_REQUESTED is a CANCEL-sibling operator lifecycle intent that drives force_release (LC2 release minus the declared-boundary gate) then purge — it is not a type: action step (no runner, no outcome routing). LC4 is storage-lifecycle ops, the L2/L2b/LC3 machinery is not involved
